findings.title: Object-level authorization missing on the invoice endpoint
findings.evidence: GET /api/invoices/4711 with the session of user 9 returns the invoice of user 3. Body redacted: [REDACTED:pii].
findings.impact: Any authenticated user reads any other tenant's invoices, including amounts and billing addresses.
findings.preconditions: A valid session on any account.
findings.recommendation: Scope the queryset to request.user at the repository layer, and add the regression test that fails without it.

severity_calibration.reason: the attacker reads invoices belonging to other tenants; their own session grants no path to that object, so the capability is new
a valid authenticated session is required and this deployment has no self-registration (settings.py:REGISTRATION_OPEN=False); ceiling high

findings.limits: Only the invoice routes were traced; the reporting module was not read.

findings.title: Update channel fetched over plain HTTP in the desktop build
findings.evidence: feedURL points at http://updates.internal.example/[REDACTED:internal-host]; no signature check is visible on the path that writes the payload.
findings.impact: An attacker on the path replaces the update payload.
findings.inference: Whether the packaged build enforces OS code signing was not observed: the signed artifact was not available.
findings.recommendation: Serve the feed over HTTPS and verify the signature against a pinned key before the payload is moved into place.

triage.reason: The notarization setting lives in the release pipeline, which is outside the audited repository; asked for the pipeline export.

findings.limits: Not reproduced against a real update server: that would require authorization.
findings.what_would_settle_it: The session middleware in `app/middleware/session.js`, which is not in the delivered scope and decides whether the token is re-verified per request.
